transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, doctor. Well, I came in today because... I've just started to feel, in a sort of quiet but stubborn way, that the best version of my life is already behind me. 

I'm usually a pretty organized person, but lately it just feels like no amount of planning or discipline is going to get me back to feeling like myself again. I just can't seem to shake that feeling, so I thought it was time to come in and talk to someone.
Have you noticed that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

No, I wouldn't say that. I still read quite a bit, and I keep up with my usual hobbies. I still enjoy them, for the most part. It's not really a loss of interest in the things I do... it's just more of that underlying feeling I mentioned.
Would you say you’re experiencing a mood that feels like a significant worsening from how you usually feel, and if so, how long has this been going on?

I wouldn't really call it a significant worsening, no. It's more that... well, this kind of just is how I usually feel now. There wasn't a sudden drop or a specific time when things got noticeably worse. It's just a steady, quiet sort of low mood. 

As for how long it's been going on, I'm not entirely sure I can put a date on it. It's just been lingering for a good while.
Can you give me a sense of how long this low mood has been present—has it been more on the scale of weeks, months, or even longer?

Well, it's definitely been longer than weeks or months. I suppose if I really trace it back, it started after I had a hiking injury. That was a little over three years ago... probably about three years and three months now, if I'm being exact. It just sort of settled in after that and never really left.
